6. Events, windows and reducers

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-06-events.Rmd
book-06-events.Rmd

What you will learn

Select records, set inclusive time windows, and reduce them to first, last, count, ever, closest, any and all values.

This chapter uses the public synthetic Synthea27Nj numeric connection from Getting started.

You need: the packages and the matching practice connection described in Before you start. Run its sections in order. Each chapter starts from a fresh practice connection; all the outputs below come from real dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4 calls. The numbers describe teaching data, not clinical findings.

Start this chapter

Start a fresh R session in the book-work directory created in Getting started. Run this setup first:

library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
source("tools/book/practice.R")
practice <- if (book_driver == "DSLite") book_practice("numeric") else book_connect("numeric")
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

The site connection is ready. The shared connection.R selects DSLite or Opal and resolves the resource names.

Define the records once

An event describes which records the server should read. These simulated hemoglobin measurements have numeric values recorded in grams per deciliter (g/dL). Concept IDs here are vocabulary inputs; they are not patient identifiers.

measure <- omop_event("measurement", concepts = 3000963L,
  value = "value_as_number", where = omop_where(unit_concept_id == 8713L))
class(measure)
#> [1] "omop_event" "list"

The unit predicate keeps values recorded in that unit; it does not convert units. Use an omop_unit() conversion when your study needs conversion.

Set a public time window

A window is an inclusive range of days around an anchor, the reference date. A fixed date works even when the population has no index event.

history <- omop_window(NULL, NULL, anchor = "2020-01-01")
class(history)
#> [1] "omop_window" "list"

Both ends are unbounded here, so every recorded measurement is eligible. For a one-year lookback use omop_window(-365, 0, anchor = "2020-01-01"); that window includes both endpoint days. An omitted window on an advanced reducer reads all history; a simple-layer shortcut usually defaults to history through the index. Choose explicitly.

First and last values

A reducer turns many records into one value per person or episode.

first <- omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("first_value", window = history))
last <- omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", window = history))
class(last)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

These select by date, source and record key, not by the size of the value. By default they skip missing values. missing = "keep" chooses the row first, so the selected row can give a missing value. With no records, both give NA.

Mean values

A mean uses all nonmissing numeric values in the window. It answers a different question from choosing the first or last recorded value.

mean_value <- omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("mean", window = history))
class(mean_value)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

The unit is still g/dL. Do not average numeric concept IDs or mixed units.

Count and ever 

n <- omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("count", window = history, distinct = "day"))
ever <- omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("binary", window = history))
class(n)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

Count measures distinct measurement days here; distinct = "row" counts records. Ever is 1 when any record exists and 0 otherwise. Neither requires a nonmissing numeric value. In a defined empty window both count and ever are zero.

Any and all test the values 

any_high <- omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("any", window = history,
    predicate = omop_where(value >= 16)))
all_high <- omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("all", window = history,
    predicate = omop_where(value >= 14)))
class(any_high)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

Ever tests whether a record exists. Any and all test a condition on its values. Here any asks about readings at least 16 g/dL; all asks whether every reading is at least 14 g/dL. Both are arbitrary teaching cutoffs, not clinical reference limits. A missing value makes its comparison unknown; a true value settles any, and a false value settles all. Otherwise an unknown remains missing. Empty windows give any = 0 and all = NA: without measurements there is no all-value result.

Assign the columns privately 

reducers <- omop_recipe(variables = list(first = first, last = last,
  mean = mean_value, days = n, ever = ever, any_high = any_high, all_high = all_high),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(reducers, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(reducers, out = c(people = "D_reducers"), conns = conns))
#>       people 
#> "D_reducers"

Only the symbol mapping returns. Request one approved aggregate at a time:

first_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_reducers$first", datasources = conns)

Value at the index

Now let the first hemoglobin measurement set a different anchor for each person. Value at index means closest within a chosen tolerance; it need not occur on the index day.

at_index <- omop_study(measure, outputs = "baseline",
  baseline = list(hemoglobin = omop_value_at_index("measurement", 3000963L,
    tolerance = c(-30, 0), unit = 8713L)))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(at_index, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(at_index, out = c(baseline = "D_at_index"), conns = conns))
#>     baseline 
#> "D_at_index"

The tolerance excludes later measurements. The shortcut uses closest_value; its default tolerance would include 90 days before and 30 days after.

at_index_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_at_index$hemoglobin", datasources = conns)
knitr::kable(book_summary(at_index_result))

Only people with an eligible hemoglobin measurement enter this indexed study. If a required anchor is missing, a window is undefined and every reducer gives NA, including count and ever.

Convert to a common unit before reducing

A numeric unit filter only restricts records. An explicit conversion normalises the values before the reducer runs. This example converts g/dL to g/L, multiplying by ten. These are the vocabulary names for the input and target units:

units <- ds.omop.concept.lookup(c(8713L, 8636L), conns = conns)
knitr::kable(units$pooled["concept_name"])
concept_name
gram per deciliter
gram per liter 
lab_gl <- omop_event("measurement", 3000963L,
  unit = omop_unit(8636L, convert = list("8713" = c(factor = 10, offset = 0))))
class(lab_gl)
#> [1] "omop_event" "list"

Rows already in g/L retain their value. Other undeclared units become missing by default; they are not guessed. A declared conversion also transforms reference ranges. Use the same target and conversion map across sites before pooling.

converted <- omop_recipe(variables = list(mean_gl = omop_variable(event = lab_gl,
  reducer = omop_reduce("mean"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(converted, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(converted, out = c(people = "D_converted"), conns = conns))
#>        people 
#> "D_converted"
conversion_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_converted$mean_gl", datasources = conns)
knitr::kable(book_summary(conversion_result))

Value bins and explicit high/low flags

A bin groups numeric values into a declared interval. These cutoffs are arbitrary teaching choices, not clinical reference ranges or treatment thresholds. We apply them to each person’s mean, privately.

print(ds.omop.mutate("D_reducers",
  band = cut(mean, breaks = c(0, 14, 15, 100),
    labels = c("below 14", "14 to below 15", "15 or above"), right = FALSE),
  high = ifelse(mean >= 15, 1L, 0L), low = ifelse(mean < 14, 1L, 0L),
  newobj = "D_lab_bins", conns = conns))
#> [1] "D_lab_bins"
bins_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_lab_bins$band", useNA = "always", datasources = conns)
knitr::kable(book_counts(bins_result))

All nonzero cells in this worked example meet the release threshold. You see the checked counts, never the private rows. A different set of bins can cause the entire table to be withheld; a refusal is not an empty or zero table. The left boundary is included and the right boundary excluded in these bins.

Recorded abnormal-high and abnormal-low counts

The dedicated reducers compare each measurement with its own range_high or range_low. They count comparable records outside those bounds.

ranges <- omop_recipe(variables = list(
  high_count = omop_variable(event = measure, reducer = omop_reduce("abnormal_high")),
  low_count = omop_variable(event = measure, reducer = omop_reduce("abnormal_low"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(ranges, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(ranges, out = c(people = "D_lab_ranges"), conns = conns))
#>         people 
#> "D_lab_ranges"
ranges_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_lab_ranges$high_count", useNA = "no", datasources = conns)
knitr::kable(book_counts(ranges_result))

Synthea27Nj has no recorded hemoglobin reference bounds. Zero here means no recorded comparable abnormal-high result; it is not evidence of normality. The study-defined flags above remain a separate, explicit definition. Never fill missing clinical reference ranges with an invented normal interval.

Recap

An event chooses records, a window chooses time, and a reducer answers one question. Empty records and an undefined anchor are different.

Try it

Add a count of measurement rows and compare its released mean and quantiles with the measurement-day summary above.

Solution

row_count <- omop_recipe(variables = list(rows = omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("count", window = history, distinct = "row"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(row_count, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(row_count, out = c(people = "D_row_count"), conns = conns))
#>        people 
#> "D_row_count"
solution_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_row_count$rows", datasources = conns)
knitr::kable(book_summary(solution_result))
